about: The SDK surface, one row per call, with the symbol each head exposes for it or null where the head does not have it yet (decision 0090). Each head's test suite checks itself against this file in both directions: every symbol named here must exist, and every public call on the facade must be named here or listed under `unlisted` with its reason, so a head can neither fall behind the manifest nor grow past it unrecorded. Checked by tacenta-client tests/surface.rs (the Rust facade's impl blocks), tacenta-ffi tests/surface.rs (the exports that become Swift and Kotlin, object by object), tooling/check-surface-bindings.sh (the generated Swift and Kotlin themselves), and sdk/typescript test/surface.test.mjs (the built package). sdk/SURFACE.md is rendered from this file by tooling/surface-grid.py, and tooling/check-surface.sh keeps the two in step. The `errors` section lists the error kinds the same way.

heads.swift: bindings/swift (crates/tacenta-ffi); the handle is `Tenant` there, since the Swift module is `Tacenta`
heads.kotlin: bindings/android (crates/tacenta-ffi); the handle is `Tenant`, for parity with Swift

objects.name: Tacenta
objects.about: One tenant's handle: built from the API key and the server's name, it fetches the service document once and hands out signed-in clients.

calls.name: connect
calls.about: Build the handle; discover the services from the server's document.

calls.name: signUp
calls.about: Create a user in the tenant.

calls.name: signIn
calls.about: Sign a user in on a device with a fresh identity; a connected client.

calls.name: signInWithState
calls.about: Sign in resuming persisted identity and sessions.

calls.name: signInWithStateSealed
calls.about: Sign in resuming sealed, rollback-resistant state with a secure store attached (decision 0078).
calls.gap: The TypeScript head has no sealed state yet.

calls.name: websocket
calls.about: Reach the services over the WebSocket carriage instead of their ports.
calls.gap: TypeScript always takes the carriage, so there is no switch.

objects.name: Client
objects.about: One signed-in user on one device.

calls.name: find
calls.about: Look a username up in the tenant.

calls.name: send
calls.about: Send to an address; the session establishes itself on first contact.

calls.name: receive
calls.about: Fetch and decrypt what is waiting.
calls.gap: Awaits the next non-empty batch on every head; inbound is the same one message at a time. A pending receive waits for mail outside the client's turn, so a send on the same client goes through meanwhile.

calls.name: inbound
calls.about: Inbound messages one at a time, as they arrive: receive flattened into the language's stream.
calls.gap: Rust: a Stream that borrows the client; TypeScript: an async iterator for `for await`; Swift: an Inbound that is an AsyncSequence; Kotlin: an Inbound with `asFlow()`. A message goes to whichever loop is running, so run one per client.

calls.name: restoreOutcome
calls.about: What the sign-in found: fresh (no sessions restored), resumed, or sessionsDiscarded (the state was older than one already seen, so its sessions were dropped and the identity kept).
calls.gap: Only the sealed restore and a checkpoint can discard sessions, so on TypeScript, which has neither, it is fresh or resumed.

calls.name: exportState
calls.about: The identity and live sessions, to persist and resume.
calls.gap: The bytes carry private keys: app-private, encrypted at rest, only the latest copy kept, and exported again after every send and receive (a restore of an older copy rewinds sessions and, on the sealed path, is refused).

calls.name: exportStateSealed
calls.gap: No sealed state on the TypeScript head yet.

calls.name: attachSecureStore
calls.about: Attach the store that makes sealed state rollback-resistant.
calls.gap: No secure-store hook on the TypeScript head yet.

calls.name: reconnect
calls.about: Re-dial the directory and relay after a drop.
calls.gap: Every head reconnects on its own with backoff; only Rust exposes the call.

objects.name: Inbound
objects.about: A client's inbound messages one at a time, on the FFI heads; Rust's Stream and TypeScript's async iterator carry their own next.

calls.name: next
calls.about: The next message, awaiting mail if none is buffered.
calls.gap: Rust and TypeScript iterate the stream itself; the Swift and Kotlin sugar is built on this call.

unlisted.about: Public calls on the facade types that are deliberately not rows of the surface: the layer under the handle, helpers, and operations no head is asked to match. Naming them here is what makes the checks two-directional; a new public call must land as a row or here.

Tacenta.connect_to: connect with a server name: a parameter of connect, not a second call (the FFI heads expose it as Tacenta.connectTo)
Tacenta.connect_via: connect with a document URL and trust: the development and private-certificate path
Tacenta.fetch_document: the discovery fetch, exposed for callers that cache documents
Tacenta.from_discovered: build from a fetched document under the origin rule
Tacenta.from_document: build from a document the caller vouches for
Tacenta.from_endpoints: build from known addresses; no discovery
Tacenta.with_connector: reach the services through caller-opened streams (the WebAssembly head's path)
Tacenta.sign_in_device: sign_in with a device number: a parameter, not a second call

Client.connect: the address layer under the handle (Config), kept for tests and deployments that know their addresses
Client.sign_up: address layer; the handle's sign_up is the row
Client.sign_in: address layer; the handle's sign_in is the row
Client.sign_in_with_state: address layer; the handle's sign_in_with_state is the row
Client.export_identity: the identity alone; export_state carries it
Client.checkpoint: rollback detection on the unsealed path (decision 0078, anchor A), opt-in
Client.rotate: signed-prekey rotation, driven by the client itself
Client.sign_in_with_state_sealed: address layer; the handle's sign_in_with_state_sealed is the row
Client.mail: the signal a head that shares the client behind a lock waits on outside the lock, then drains; receive is that loop

ffi.about: Keyed by export: `Object.method` for a method or constructor, a bare name for a free function.
ffi.sign_up: address layer, plaintext; the handle's signUp is the row
ffi.sign_up_tls: address layer, TLS; the handle's signUp is the row
ffi.Client.connect: the address layer under the handle (Config)
ffi.Client.sign_in: address layer, plaintext; the handle's signIn is the row
ffi.Client.sign_in_tls: address layer, TLS; the handle's signIn is the row
ffi.Client.sign_in_with_state: address layer; the handle's signInWithState is the row
ffi.Client.sign_in_with_state_sealed: address layer; the handle's signInWithStateSealed is the row
ffi.Client.export_identity: the identity alone; export_state carries it
ffi.Tenant.connect_via: connect with a document URL: the local development path

errors.about: Every head raises one error type whose kind an app branches on: Rust `Error::kind()` gives an `ErrorKind` (and `as_str()` its name as the other heads spell it); TypeScript throws `TacentaError` with a `kind` and the detail in `message`; Swift throws `ClientError` with one case per kind and the detail in `reason`; Kotlin throws `ClientException` with one subclass per kind and the detail in `reason`. The kind is the contract and may gain members, so handle the ones you branch on and let the rest fall through; the detail is a string for a log line, not for matching on. Checked by the same tests as the calls.

kinds.name: Network
kinds.about: The network or the transport failed; retry later.

kinds.name: Discovery
kinds.about: The service document could not be fetched or read.

kinds.name: UnknownTenant
kinds.about: The API key selects no tenant.

kinds.name: UsernameTaken
kinds.about: The username is already taken in this tenant.

kinds.name: InvalidUsername
kinds.about: The username is not one the server accepts.

kinds.name: SignUpRefused
kinds.about: A sign-up was refused for another reason: registration is closed, or the handle is reserved.

kinds.name: SignInRefused
kinds.about: The credentials were refused, or the session expired; coarse by design.

kinds.name: IdentityMismatch
kinds.about: The address is bound to a different device identity (trust on first use); also a sealed state offered to a user or device it was not sealed for.

kinds.name: RateLimited
kinds.about: The server asked for a slower pace: too many failed sign-ins, or the recipient's queue is full. Back off and retry.

kinds.name: ServerFailure
kinds.about: The server could not process the request; nothing was applied. Retry.

kinds.name: State
kinds.about: The persisted state was refused: altered, older than the last send, or its secure-storage key is wrong; whatever else a SecureStore raises surfaces here. Do not delete the blob.

kinds.name: StoreUnavailable
kinds.about: The platform's secure store could not be reached (a Keychain before first unlock, a Keystore that needs the user). Nothing was refused: retry after unlock and keep the blob.

kinds.name: InvalidArgument
kinds.about: The caller's own input was wrong: a malformed address or config, a message over the size limit.

kinds.name: Internal
kinds.about: A protocol or cryptographic failure, or a bug: worth reporting.
